newsitem.title: USA: NABL urges revisions to IRS private activity rules.
newsitem.headline: NABL urges revisions to IRS private activity rules.

text.p: The National Association of Bond Lawyers warned IRS Monday that a key provision in its final private activity bond regulations is unworkable and "unduly punitive."

The rules, which took effect May 15, give issuers detailed guidance on a requirement in the Tax Reform Act of 1986 that says no more than 10 percent of a public-purpose tax-exempt bond issue can benefit from private business.

One of the rule's provisions says that if a locality changes the use of a bond financed project -- from one that qualifies for tax exemption to one that does not -- it must redeem or defease every dollar of the private use.
"It's kind of like a cliff," said bond lawyer Mitchell Rapaport, who helped write the NABL comment letter.

"If you go a penny over the private use percentage limit, you have to redeem or defease bonds equal to every dollar of private use rather than just the excess," Rapaport said in a telephone interview.
"The measure of unqualified bonds is unduly punitive, analytically unsound, a radical departure from existing change-of-use principles, and unworkable," NABL said in its 28-page comment letter.

The letter, principally drafted by John Cross, chairman of NABL's general tax matters committee, said the provision is particularly a problem for large-scale financings that involve numerous projects.
"We strongly urge reconsideration of this principle," the letter said.
NABL said, overall, most of the new rules are "sound and workable."
